text:
maya: heads up — reproducible perf regression on canary when selector routes to flashattn_v3 for causal runs with warm KV cache. ~18% throughput drop on gpt-like workload.

jon: which canary? paste the trace?

maya: canary id=canary/rdw-57 on dedicated pool. quick summary from perf-bot: 

perf-bot: Auto-profile summary:
```
model: gpt-3b-like
kernel_selected: flashattn_v3 (causal path)
seq_len: 128 (query) with cached_prefix ~384 -> effective kv_len ~384
head_dim: 64
batch: 8
baseline_throughput: 160 tokens/s
observed_throughput: 131 tokens/s  # -18%
lat_p50: 10ms -> 12.4ms
mem_bw_util: up 22%
cache_hit_ratio: 0.92
```

maya: attaching a couple of tiny perf traces (stack-ish):
```
CPU: driver queues spike at kv_append
GPU: flashattn_v3::causal_kernel_fastpath -> falls back to slower block in inner loop when kv_page unaligned
smashed memcpy ops between KV writes
```

liang: interesting. v3 has more aggressive fusion for non-causal and assumes aligned KV pages for head_dim multiples of 128-ish. with head_dim=64 v3 sometimes uses a different tiling that expects contiguous KV layout; warm cache + prefix concat can create small misaligned fragments. that could force extra copies.

eva: did we try forcing flashattn_v2 or v1 for the same canary?

maya: forced v2 for the same job -> regression disappeared; throughput back to baseline + ~2%. so seems routing choice is the culprit, not a model change.

samir: two hypotheses: (1) selector currently only considers seq_len and model family, not kv_cache length or cache_hit_ratio, (2) v3 heuristics need a head_dim / alignment check. either/both could flip us to a suboptimal kernel.

jon: agree. low-effort mitigation: include kv_cache_length in selector decision. e.g. compute effective_seq = max(query_seq_len, avg_cached_prefix_len) and route based on that.

liang: we should be careful: computing avg_cached_prefix_len per-request is cheap if we keep it in the request metadata (we already emit kv_len to tracing). propose selector change:
```
# pseudo
effective_kv = request.kv_len if request.kv_len else 0
effective_seq = max(request.query_len, effective_kv)
if request.causal:
  if head_dim % 128 == 0 and effective_seq < 256:
    choose flashattn_v3
  elif effective_seq >= 256:
    choose flashattn_v2
  else:
    choose flashattn_v1
else:
  choose flashattn_v3
```

samir: also add an alignment guard: if head_dim not divisible by 32/64 boundary expected by the kernel, prefer v1/v2. we've seen head_dim=48 previously hit a slowpath.

eva: add tests: microbench matrix that sweeps head_dim {48,64,80,96}, seq {64,128,256,512}, kv_len {0,64,256,384}, batch {1,8}. check throughput + memory copy counts.

maya: ran quick microbench (local) and saw head_dim=48 + kv_len>=256 -> v3 gives -25% throughput vs v2. attaching short table from local run:
```
head_dim,kv_len,selector,throughput
48,0,v3,145
48,256,v3,108  # bad
48,256,v2,138  # good
64,384,v3,131  # bad seen on canary
64,384,v2,160  # baseline
```

jon: ok actionable list?

liang: I'll implement selector change to compute effective_seq and add two guards: (1) prefer v2 when effective_seq >= 256 for causal, (2) prefer v1/v2 when head_dim not aligned to kernel assumption. I'll add unit tests and the microbench matrix.

samir: add a temporary runtime flag to force kernel routing override for canary groups so we can roll fixes without full release.

maya: created ENGRT-2245 with details + microbench results, assigned to liang, linked canary, added steps to revert if no improvement.

eva: also add a perf regression alert rule: if throughput drops >10% vs baseline for same model/kernel within canary, auto-add a high-priority incident.

maya: thanks — let's run the matrix overnight and pick a patch tomorrow morning. will update thread when I have results. :thumbsup:
